EntityProps.Definition:
A method for calculation of GHG emissions resulting from the use of a fuel. A method may be either an input method or an output method. Input methods use a given quantity of fuel consumed. Output methods calculate the quantity of fuel consumed to achieve a designated output from a given equipment consumption rate. An example of an output method is vehicle distance where the fuel consumed is calculated from a given distance and vehicle mileage rate.
Sets of consumption rates are defined for application equipment types and fuel products that can be applied to one or more regions.
EntityProps.Name: APPLICATION_METHOD
EntityProps.Comment:

Sets of consumption rates are defined for application equipment types and fuel products that can be applied to one or more regions.

EntityProps.Definition:
A type of part of the whole life GHG emission footprint of a product, used to account for all the direct and indirect GHG emissions involved with the creation, distribution, use and disposal of a product.
For example: WtT (well to tank) covers the GHG emissions footprint arising from the manufacture and distribution of a product. This includes the emissions from the production and transformation of natural resources into raw materials of the product manufacturing process. TtW (tank to wheel) covers the use or consumption of the product.

EntityProps.Definition: Maps the parameters of a client product type to corresponding IDs depending on the type of parameter. Parameters can be of 2 types - Carbon Intensity and Property Conversion factor. If parameter type is Carbon Intensity Factor, the field Activity_Type_Param_ID points to the corresponding CI factor. This can be then used to fetch the emission factors for the client product type If parameter type is Conversing Factor, the field Property_Value_ID points to Product_Property_Value table. This is used to return the corresponding property value

EntityProps.Definition: Maps the parameters of a client product type to corresponding IDs depending on the type of parameter. Parameters can be of 2 types - Carbon Intensity and Property Conversion factor. If parameter type is Carbon Intensity Factor, the field Activity_Type_Param_ID points to the corresponding CI factor. This can be then used to fetch the emission factors for the client product type If parameter type is Conversion Factor, the field Property_Value_ID points to Fuel_Product_Property_Value table. This is used to return the corresponding property value
